utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: On the 2nd of October, 1998, Bellanice and Banje were within the 121st Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we were at the phase of the restructuring the brigade in various parts, in various areas, and this was the case also for the 121st Brigade. That part fell under the command of that brigade, as you said. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So the answer is yes, they were in the 121st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. They were intended to be part of the -- covered by the Brigade 121st.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, were they in the brigade or were they not in the brigade on the 2nd of October, 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me to explain, I will explain. They were under the Brigade 121st, but after the August offensive, as I told you, soldiers or members or the structures of the KLA were reorganised. Various units were in Bellanice, Blace, Banje. A number of surrendered their weapons or they had withdrawn. So we had to restructure the KLA in those areas where the Serb police were still operating --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, by the 2nd of October, 1998, several months later, those villages, your testimony is that they were in the 121st Brigade. You're nodding your head yes. In fact --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In fact -- let me ask you another question. In fact, the son of Ramiz Hoxha, Enver Hoxha, was a soldier in the 121st Brigade at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I wanted to clarify. The units that had remained from the past was -- were still being reconstructed, and the area you're referring to was still under Serb control, and we were not able act and operate in Bellanice or in Temeqine or in Blace because the Serbian forces were positioned at Malisheve, at Duhle, and they were moving uninterruptably along that line. At that time this was an area which was not controlled by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But it fell under the area that the 121st Brigade was interested in.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Ramiz Hoxha and Selman Binici did not work for the Serb police of the UDB, did they?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can speak of Selman Binici. He is a friend of mine from school. We are the same generation. We had good contacts with him, and I maintained these contacts even after we completed school. He helped me on different occasions with different things, economically and so on. We were not only schoolmates but we also visited families. I visited his and he visited mine. And I never heard that Binici was a collaborator with the Serbs. Even when he was killed, I didn't hear that he had been a collaborator. As for Mr. Hoxha, Your Honours, I already told you that I grew up in Bellanice. In other words, I had family ties there, and I knew most of this village. Ramiz, I knew him because he was nephew in our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He was never a member of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before he was executed on the 2nd of October, he was one of nine men who represented his village in peace negotiations with the Serb authorities after the Serb offensive; right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. Maybe there were nine, 12, or 13. It could be that Ramiz was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about this case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And on the 2nd of October, they were kidnapped from their villages, driven to a road and executed. You're nodding your head yes. Ramiz Hoxha was cut on the right side of his face and he was shot in the chest. Selman Binici had his skull broken. Right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. I've seen two of the bodies, Your Honours, and this is not true. The reason I've seen the bodies is that I was there myself along the road where the bodies were, and it's not true that they were in the state that you describe it. I just saw that they had been shot by a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's all. They were just shot by a weapon. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was that I didn't see anything apart from the fact that they were dead, executed. I didn't check their bodies. The position that these bodies were lying, they had nothing on them except for bullet shots. I didn't see anything else. I didn't see anything what Mr. Prosecutor is saying. I don't know what the later analysis showed. Maybe I am mistaken, but what I've seen is what I've described just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you examine the bodies closely, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, Mr. Prosecutor, the situation was really tense. We were in a shock and things can be forgotten. I think that a person, a close relative of Ramiz, turned his body on the other side. Maybe I am mistaken, but this person turned the body. And I again would like to stress that I did not see the things that you have described. Personally, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: There was a note left next to their bodies which read and I'll read it it's in evidence, P184, and the note said, it was from the Kosovo Liberation Army, from the Secret Police Service Centre: "In the name of the people," and it's an "order of the execution for the collaboration with the invaders." "For the anti-Albanian propaganda and for the spread of fear, panic and hatred in the name of the Albanian people and in the name of our liberation war, we sentence Ramiz Hoxha to death as a traitor of our nation. The same thing will happen to all the other traitors." So, Mr. Limaj, it's not true, is it, that collaborators were only people who worked for the Serb police?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You, Mr. Prosecutor, cannot give an answer without hearing to the very end the case of these two persons. You have to listen my testimony to the very end. The letter that you've just read, Your Honours, I've seen this letter next to the bodies of these two persons. It was a piece of paper with extraordinary, not very ordinary writing, probably written by someone who was not well educated. But you should listen to my answer to the very end, what I have heard about this incident, because it is in my interest, too, to clarify things about this case as there were many speculations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm interested in your complete answer, Mr. Limaj, I am. But this was done by the KLA, wasn't it? You've already told us that. You're nodding --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you've also told us that neither of these people worked for the police.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to that time, I had never heard that these two persons, Your Honour, and for the sake of the truth and for the sake what I've -- what I know, up to that time I had never heard that these two persons were collaborators or members of any Serb police units. I don't know about the other person, but for Ramiz because he worked in Slovenia for some time. But as for Mr. Binici, I know that person. He was there the night I fled from Serb forces. If you remember Your Honours, I said that I was staying with a family --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You're changing the subject now. You're talking about something different. Let's talk about this. So what you said earlier, it's not true that collaborators were only people who worked for the Serb police; is that right? Yes or no? It was not true?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot get my answer on this question unless you hear me out. I would like to explain everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why don't you give an answer and then give your explanation?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because things that I heard later on showed that these two persons were implicated in a case. At least this is the information I got, because I was directly interested in this case. I think this is important for Their Honours to know. At least for Selman I wanted to know what had happened, what did he do. And out of this interest I got an information, a complete information which I find important to share it here with you, and I think that I should state what kind of information I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll give you an opportunity to state that information, but -- but you did not learn later that they had worked for the Serb police, did you?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later I learned of a very grave case which is directly linked with the Serbian police, and I'm stressing here that I heard about this case, and it's important for me to mention it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, before you give that explanation, let's look at the way the KLA itself described why these people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And again, this is in evidence. It's in evidence in two different places, but one place is P184, because there were several newspaper articles. There was a communique issued on the 5th of November, 1998, and I'll read from the one in Koha Ditore. It's up on Sanction I note in the translation the date is wrong. It says 5 at the present time but it's actually 5 November in the one attached. It says -- I'm reading this communique. It says, "According to the KLA Information Service Directorate's information, in their activities against the KLA's war of liberation the above made" -- and this is referring to different people, Cen Desku and Jakup Kastrati, "the above made propaganda in favour of handing over of weapons in cooperation with collaborators Selman Binici from Banje village and Ramiz Hoxha from Bellanice village. Executed earlier by the KLA. As well as being in long-term coordination with Agim Krasniqi, a member of the LDK Presidency who is also known to the KLA Information Service as an instigator of special warfare against the KLA and the founder of a sort of Kosovo police in support of autonomy."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: There's nothing in there from Selman Binici working for the Serb police, is there? You're shaking your head.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: They were not executed because they worked for the Serb police, were they?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, this is important. This interlinks with other things, and that's why I think it's important that you hear me out. This is at least what I was told and why they concretely didn't say what led to that case. At that time, I was exercising a continuous pressure on the General Staff to get information how these people were killed, because these two people I knew very well. They were in the terrain. The murder was committed in the terrain covered by my brigade. We wanted to know what was going on. Now we had the borderline as envisaged to be covered by the brigade, and it was in our interest to find out what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I wonder if I might intervene. He's been promised the opportunity to give his explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I know, Mr. Mansfield. I'm well alert and I'm waiting, but I think it can't be said it's being denied yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, why don't you explain what you learned.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Your Honours, maybe it would be appropriate for the sake of their families to go into a private session. Personally, I don't mind speaking in an open session, but just to consider the names that will be mentioned. But it's very important because this has to do with a rape, and that's why maybe it would be appropriate to go in private session. If not, I can speak of this in public session as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know what's coming. Out of an abundance of caution we should go into private session. We can always make it public later if that's appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So, Mr. Limaj, your testimony is that when you spoke to Sokol Bashota and Rexhep Selimi and Kadri Veseli and all the members of the General Staff they didn't tell you that this was the reason for the murder but that you heard this from somebody else, this Mensur Zyberi from Rahovec. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that when I went to the members of the General Staff, I sought an explanation whether they were killed by the KLA. The KLA should assume responsibility for that. Otherwise, we should find the culprits.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... did assume responsibility for it, didn't it? Isn't that correct? They did assume responsibility for it in a communique?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, Sokol and Kadri told me that we would investigate the case. We will see what happened. And then after that they issued the communique, the General Staff. After the information came.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So your testimony is that they issued this communique to cover up the real reason for the murder. That's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, because it was a sensitive matter. We didn't want the Albanians to be decked out as persons who could do this with the Serb forces. It was debasing for the KLA communique to present Albanians in such a light. This is what they thought best.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the note that was left by the body, that was not part of this cover-up, was it? Because that was left at the time they were killed.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw -- I saw the nod with my own eyes. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And this, as you say, was within your brigade. Did you do anything? Aside from talking to the General Staff, did you yourself do anything to investigate this? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, after the information I received and when the General Staff assumed responsibility for that, I considered the issue closed, that there was nothing else I could do. It was not my responsibility, because I knew this was an act not committed by my soldiers, that we had nothing to do with it. And I considered it as closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It was an act committed by KLA soldiers in your zone, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not committed in my zone. The people were taken, if I might say, in my territory. They had gone to another territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I see. So because they were kidnapped in your territory and murdered in another territory you thought that you didn't need to investigate it? Not your matter? Not for you to worry about?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, on the contrary. I think I told you that I did my job. Just because they were people from my territory, I inquired. Had I not done what I did, maybe what happened wouldn't have happened. Those people -- the General Staff assumed responsibility for the act, and I felt that I no longer could do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just because they were from my territory that I inquired after what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said there was --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't do more at that time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, did you ever go talk to their families?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You go.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who did you talk to in the families?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I am not wrong, on the next day -- I think, yes, it was the next day. I went to Selman Binici's family. I met with his brothers and parent and talked, and they asked me about what had happened, and nobody knew. And I told them that just like you I know nothing. His father asked me, Do you know if my son did anything wrong? And I answered, Not as far as I know. You know I was his friend, and I expressed my condolences, because my family was a neighbour to Selman's house. They were divided by a wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, after you found out the information that you learned from Mensur Zyberi from Rahovec, did you then go back to the families of Ramiz Hoxha or Selman Binici to see if it could possibly be true?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, after the General Staff had assumed responsibility for what happened, I did not go to these families.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Nobody went to the families, did they?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Nobody investigated these allegations, did they?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did my share of work, as I told you. I couldn't do more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now -- you couldn't do that, more than that, or you chose not to do more than that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, you do not know what the situation was in September 1998 in Kosova, especially in that area. There was total confusion. Following the September offensive, it was impossible to move about. I think that was the first move, I think, end of September, beginning of October, when I went to visit my family after all what had happened in August. It was, as I said, total confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you because you're talking about yourself again and I want to talk about these families. Nobody ever went and talked to them. A year later, Ramiz Hoxha's son Fadil Hoxha published an article in the newspaper other saying that there was never any trial or any kind of hearing or procedures or anything, and that is also in evidence. It's P184. It's attached to Enver Hoxha's statement. That's true. There was never any investigation; right? Not then, not a year later, never.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. At least I don't know. I know as far as what I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the truth, Mr. Limaj, is that these men weren't killed for those reasons that you gave the Court but they were killed because they were perceived for whatever reason as not being loyal to the KLA. Isn't that true? Exactly what is said in the statements in the note left by their body and in the newspaper article. That's why they were killed, isn't it, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot accept that, because I have many more reasons to believe what I was told at that time. I cannot accept what you are putting to me, because since you are saying that no investigations were carried out, I told you the only information I had at that time. These people came from another region, and I had no reason to suspect that these people wanted to do something -- some harm to others. That's why I believed what I was told, because they came from another region. If they were from Banje, then I would have reason to believe that there was some other underlying motive. But the person who told me didn't know anything, just as people he had seen with his eyes. At least that's what he told me. That's why I believed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's look now at the communiques, because you've talked about them and let's actually look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: For that purpose I'm going to ask that you provided P48 and P49, and P48 we can provide in the large format which is easier to read. That's P48, the large format. But he'll also need P49, even for him, because I think there's a translation of one of them that's in P49. I can actually provide the first one. If we could provide this. I'm going to turn our attention first to the first page of P49. In English it's communique from 20 May 1997. It's U0038552, and I have the Albanian translation here. It's one that is not contained in P48. So if that could be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, here's and communicate from the 20th of May, 1997. It's communique number 33. It's when you were in Switzerland; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to -- I'm just going to focus on the second sentence, which is: "In a press release, communique number 33, faxed to the media, the UCK said that it killed Hetem Dobruna at Llozice village at Klina earlier this month because of his notorious and open collaboration with the Serbian occupying authorities." Now, there's nothing in that communique, is there, about him working for the Serb police or the UDB, is there?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that doesn't mean that he hasn't worked for them. This in my opinion doesn't prove anything. I think you can prove who he was, whether that is true or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, you testified earlier that there were clear instructions in the KLAs -- I mean in the communiques.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And there are no clear instructions in this communique, are there?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may not be here, but you have other communiques that contained such instructions. You have them in your evidence. There are such, many I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's look at the other communiques.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to turn to communique number 35, and in the English it is U0038554 in P49. In the Albanian it's page 1607 at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You see the numbers at the top, Mr. Limaj? Maybe the usher needs to provide assistance. It's U0081607. It should be Koha Ditore from 8 August 1997.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 16 -- what did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: 607. On the Albanians it's in the upper left. It says: "By decision of the UCK Central Staff made on 3 and 4 August, our guerrilla units carried out three armed operations against the occupiers and their collaborators." And then it talks about two assassinations of two individuals. And again, there's nothing there, is there, about them working for the police or being in the UDB?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true. It doesn't say anything about these two persons. It doesn't explicitly say that they have worked, but I think that most of the communiques do contain such instructions. In the case of Ramiz Leku, I have heard -- I don't know he's -- I have heard that this person continuously participated in murder operations, raids of the inhabitants. For Ali Qullapeku, I haven't heard anything. For Ramiz Leku, this is known all over Drenica that he was a notorious person. Why the communiques have not written everything -- it depends who wrote it. Your Honours, it depends who wrote the communiques, what the person who formulated them thought. But in the case of Ramiz Leku, we all know who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did he work for the Serb police of the UDB?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramiz Leku always worked with the Serb police. He was paid by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying again that this is what his co-villagers, people who knew him very well said in the area he operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, after March, people talked. There are tens of comrades I have from Drenica. I went to visit the village and we saw each other. I saw Ramiz Keqina who is a martyr now. Ramiz Leku beat him and his family and tens of other families. One of the members was almost paralysed. I remember him --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the communique in August 1997, did you know it then? You didn't, did you? You shook your head.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA had come out as a force to liberate and serve its people and not to kill Albanians. It was normal for us to believe in the KLA. The public appearance regarding these operations, it was public because if innocent people were killed, the KLA would never have had enjoyed the support amongst the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, it didn't depend on who wrote the communique. It depended on who the person was who was being killed. Some people were killed for being in the police and others were killed simply for talking to the police too much or for being accused of giving evidence or for being suspected. Isn't that true, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I don't rule out the possibility that such things occurred. But the majority, I'm referring to the period when there was communiques -- we have seen from the communiques that people were killed. I do not rule out the possibility that someone who was suspected of being with the police was killed, but at that time what I believed was that people -- there were clear instructions about these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In fact, it was just as Mr. Krasniqi testified here, wasn't it, that people who were suspected of causing damage to the country were considered collaborators. Isn't that true, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said yesterday, day before yesterday, Malisheve comprises of 53 villages. Why any such case occurred in Malisheve until that time. As I said, there were many people who had spent time with the Serb police in cafeterias and nothing befell on them. I didn't see in the villages of my area a person who was killed just because of spending time with Serb policemen in a cafeteria. And imagine the Malisheve municipality consists of 53 villages, and nothing occurred in these villages of this kind. And on this I base my standpoint. If at that time in 1997, 1998, an innocent person was killed, at least the area where that action occurred would know that something is wrong and that there would be a reaction, and the reaction by the population shows that these people were not what you think, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, I think the reaction is why you are in court here today. The communique, if you could open it up again, also says that the -- if you could look at it again, that same communique. It says that the KLA is -- it says: "Because we are dealing with an enemy that understands nothing but the language of force, we are compelled to talk down the barrel of a gun not as terrorists but as a liberation organisation." Right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it also says at the bottom that: "The UCK draws the attention of the international community to its failure to make a tangible commitment to solving the issue of Albanian lands in the former Yugoslavia." So as early as August 1997, the KLA is seeking the support of the international community; right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. But the risk that we were running was that from the actions it could be labelled as a terrorist organisation, and this had already started.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's look at communique number 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's U0038557 in the English, and in the Albanian it is 1608.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You're familiar with this communique, aren't you, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read the communiques, and I followed all the communiques published in this period, but I don't know what the reference is here, because at that time, as you know, the only way to communicate with the public was through communiques. We even used to read communiques in public rallies and gatherings just to let the population know that the KLA existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in fact, a copy of this communique was found in your house when your house was searched at the time of your arrest. It's Exhibit P26.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. It must be from the public information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, in this communique it says that "On the evening of the 20th of November, Dalip Dugolli, a collaborator and one of Milosevic's most trusted men, was killed in the village of Petrastica near Stimlje." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It doesn't say anything -- it doesn't say anything about Mr. Dugolli being in the police or UDB, does it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say that he was a policeman or an UDB member, but this does not exclude the possibility that he did collaborate with the Serbian police. And after all, Dragan Jasovic proved this, and it's exactly in relation to this person we are speaking of here. I never saw or heard of this person. Of course at that time I was in Switzerland. But this does not exclude the possibility that he did participate directly in the operations launched by the Serb police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You had no information, did you, that he was a member of the police or the UDB?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Switzerland at that time, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So the answer is no, you had no information.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't know him, and I didn't know anything of this. But I heard here from Jasovic for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You didn't hear that he was a -- served in the police, did you?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that the notorious policeman Jasovic, who had continuous contacts with Dalip, with the forest ranger. And for these reasons it is possible that this person have -- worked for the police. But as I said, this is just possible. I'm just speculating because I don't know about this, and I don't have any information about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So even today you're still speculating and you have no information; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not speculating. I'm just saying that I don't know. And you are on the same wave with me because you cannot know either. Only those who committed it can know. Personally, I don't know. And I can not answer for each and every member of the KLA what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No clear instructions from the KLA, were there?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me they were clear, very clear, to my opinion. And this was discussed thousands of times. I have participated for a year in a row [as interpreted] in public information rallies. We would get these statements. We would discuss them with the citizens, discussing how our war would develop, and everything was clear. And now maybe not all knew and had it clear. But you as well know that there were people who were active and in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Limaj, but I thought that at the beginning of this session you testified that the only way this information was communicated about collaborators was through the communiques. Are you now saying that it was communicated some other way, in rallies?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I said is the following: When we would discuss during gatherings regarding fund-raising, we of course discussed the importance of war, the goals, how things will develop, how that was a just war, that that was not a terrorist war, that our goals were very clear, that the war was necessary, and the only alternative that the KLA was going to fight the Serb police and those directly involved in the crimes committed by the Serb forces. This were things that we discussed with the citizens, because we needed to raise funds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But, Mr. Limaj, you did not get instructions about -- clear instructions about collaborators and what collaborators were in those rallies or fund-raising, did you? That's not your testimony, is it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I gave my answer to this question. At that time while we were in Switzerland, from the reactions, citizens' reactions, you could see what was going on. When we returned to Kosova it was clear what our activity was going to be, and I think I have answered your question already two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You will forgive me if I differ but I'll move on. On the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Whiting, is that a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I have just one other sentence to draw his attention to in the communique and then perhaps we can break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In the same communique it says: "We repeat to the international centres that we are interested in this peninsula that our struggle is the just struggle of liberation. It is the occupier who is waging a war of terrorism." And that's what you and the KLA believed at that time, is that right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that true this communique the KLA wanted to show its activities, that it wasn't a terrorist organisation. And, Your Honours, it was the only way to communicate with the public, through communiques. Even as far as I remember in 1997, the Serbs had launched a propaganda before the international community to proclaim the KLA a terrorist organisation. And this -- if -- had the KLA been called as a terrorist organisation, this would have been suicidal for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think that's a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, if we could turn now to communique number 42. It's in your -- in your version it's on 1610.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In English it's on 8560 in P48. It's a communique from the 28th of February, 1998. 1610.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You see it's in the top in the middle. About halfway down it says: "On 13 February 1990," and I believe that's a typographical error. It should be 1998, Mustafe Kurti, a collaborator with the occupier, was liquidated." Do you see that, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Nothing there about him being a member of the police or the UDB, is there?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have information about this person as well which I can present here before Your Honours. This person is from Obrinje village, who was directly connected to the Serbian police. In his house, the communication line with the Serb police was established, because the village of Obrinje is very close to the Serbian police station in Likovc. In 1997, the entire system of communication was found in his house. As I know, in this period two KLA soldiers were injured in the -- on the road Kline-Obrinje, and in this operation Mustafe Kurti participated with the Serb police. And not only Mustafe Kurti but two or three of his brothers were also connected with the Serb police. I think they publicly joined the Serb police forces during the war, during the operations in Drenica. So he was a member of a family who was in direct connections with the Serbian police. This is information that I got after 1998, maybe in April. I'm not quite sure about the time, but I think it was around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. But first of all, it's not clear at all -- this information that you claim to have, it's not at all contain in the communique, is it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was clear to all the people in that region. I think it was clear for them. This is what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But it wasn't clear to you when you read the communique, was it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any reasons not to believe what was said in the communique.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You also --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because not everyone can know whether it is true or not. I didn't know these persons either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Precisely. Mr. Limaj, you've also said two different things. You've said that you thought that they were connected to the Serb police, and then you kind of threw in that you thought they were openly working for the Serb police. He was not an employee of the Serb police, was he? He was not a Serb -- he was not an employee of the Serb police, was he?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I'm sorry to hear what you're saying because the citizens are listening. I did not say that. This person was known to entire Drenica that he was an active person in cooperation with the Serb police. I told you that the soldiers found the entire apparatus of communication in his house. This is not what I've seen personally, but this is what I heard, and everyone in Drenica knows of this person. Not only of him but also of his two or three brothers who also worked with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So your testimony is that he was considered a collaborator because he cooperated with the Serb police. Is that your testimony, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said, Your Honours, earlier, and I'm repeating myself: This person directly participated in the wounding of those two or three soldiers that I mentioned, but he also participated directly in Likoshan and Qirez massacres together with some other Albanians. He was an active member of the Serbian police. He was the person in which -- in whose house this communication system was found, and this proves his position. Another person later on was killed as well. To my knowledge, these people don't live there any longer, and this shows how active they were with the Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, I have to press this point because I suggest your answer is not clear. You are -- it is because of the communication equipment in their house that they were considered to be cooperators with the Serb police. That's what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Are you saying that this man was a employee of the Serb police, that he was a member of the Serb police himself? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an active participant with the Serbian police and army, and I took the example with the communication equipment just to illustrate his activity. This was my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And are you aware -- aside from the communication equipment, are you aware of any other activity that this man participated in?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this happened after the KLA became public in those parts, that is to say in Obrinje and Likovc. According to what the others have seen, this person was active in the preparation of activities that the Serb regime undertook in Likoshan, Prekaz and Qirez. And together with Lutfi Havazi -- or Ijazi [phoen], I don't remember his last name -- this is a fact. This person directly fought the KLA forces. He, together with his brothers. This person, to the with his three brothers, directly fought against the KLA members. This I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, you have testified that he participated directly in Likoshan and Qirez massacres. That's what you said. I'm reading it from the computer.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I've heard is that he took part in the preparation of the activities and the massacres in Qirez and Likoshan because this was an extraordinary case. This is amongst the rarest cases of persons who -- where fighting occurred, where there was direct fighting with the soldiers. And this was known to the public. Occurred sometime in April.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, he was killed on the 13th of February, 1998. That's before the massacres in Likoshan and Qirez.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I described how active his family was. He, together with his three brothers. He participated directly, and as a result of the activities in Likoshan and in Prekaz, his family, himself and his brothers, fought directly with the KLA members. He was killed before the activities in Likoshan and Qirez, but his activities continued because the preparations for the massacres at Likoshan and Qirez could not be done in one day. This is what I know. And for the developments in April, we are witnesses to that. We heard that because we could move at that time. We could go to Likovc. And to go to Likovc, you have to go through Obrinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, at the time he was killed, even if it were true that he were involved in preparation of those massacres, that could not have been known. You agree with that; right? That was not known at the time he was killed.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: People knew that he was an active member of the KLA -- correction, Serbian police and army. This is true that people knew. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You did not know that, did you?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. Personally, I don't know this person even today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Exactly. Further down on the communique it says, "We welcome the increased interest of the international community and especially U.S. and Franco-German diplomacy and declare that a solution to the Albanian question cannot be confined to the present borders of Kosova." Again, an appeal for international support; right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we turn to a speech that Jakup Krasniqi gave. It's P141.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If that could be provided to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: On the second page in the English and the Albanian, it says -- this is a speech that Jakup Krasniqi gave at a funeral for the victims of Qirez and Likoshan. It says "We also warn the international mechanisms - the UN, the Security Council, the USA, the EU and European Parliament, et cetera, to respect the charters and documents which they themselves drafted and signed from the Atlantic one to that of Helsinki and Paris. "We are fully confident that in none of the mentioned valid documents can the defending of one's national threshold and dignity be assessed as a terrorist act, and that not a single liberation war in any country of the world has been qualified as a terrorist one. And our war is nothing but a liberation one. If we chose to exercise terrorism, we would surely do it in Serbia and not in our homes." That was the position of the KLA, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the sake of the truth -- I don't know in what capacity Mr. Krasniqi delivered this speech, but vision presented here is a vision of the KLA. That's a fact. I can't ascertain here whether he gave that on behalf of the KLA spokesperson as an activist or as a member, but the things mentioned here are things constantly mentioned in the communiques of the KLA and the political statements. I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could turn to communique number 45. It's that -- in that large format. It's 1612 and in English it's 8566. It's from the 11th of March, 1998. 1612, yes. It's on the bottom right and it says almost at the bottom it says, "We ask the world's capitals to recognise the state of Kosova and punish the Serbian occupier on the international conventions of war, because Serbia's fascist war to annihilate the Albanian people is now plain." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Give me a second to find it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that also expresses the view of the KLA; right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Turn, please, to communique number 47. It's 1614, and in English it's 8573 of P48. In Albanian it's at the top of the page and it's published in Koha Ditore an on the 13th of May, 1998. And I want to read at the beginning. It says: "On the orders of the UCK General Staff successive operations against the invasion troops were carried out in Operational Zone Number 1, that is in the operational subzones of Drenica, Erenik, Dukagjin, Pastrik, and Llap." It also says, "Throughout this period operations were also carried out against Albanian collaborationists who despite earlier warnings did not abandon their anti-national courses of action." Now, my first question is this is dated the 13th of May, 1998. So the operational zones are already conceived. Pashtrik Operational Zone already exists, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. Not the Drenica zone was formed as a zone, not to speak about Pashtrik [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's say that the operational zones, or subzones as they are termed in this communique, are at least planned and conceived of; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I agree to that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Recalling that this is on the 13th of May, 1998, it says -- part-way down in the communique, it says: "In a lightning as by our military formations, an operation again the enemy's punitive expeditions on the main road in the operational subzone of Pashtrik was successful carried out." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Do you see that, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Operational Zone of Erenik. Not Pashtrik, Erenik. If I'm correctly following, it some -- successful operations were carried out in the Erenik zone, subzone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. I'm talking further down, Mr. Limaj. It says "In a lightning action --"

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise then, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: -- enemy's punitive expeditions on the main road in the operational subzone of Pashtrik was successfully carried out." Do you see that? Take your time.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me a second. There is a cluster of names of subzones. "With a rapid operation we managed to successfully carry out an operation in the Pashtrik subzone, operational subzone." Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You're looking at the top of the third column?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm talking about the main road in Pashtrik.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's a reference to the battle of the 9th of May in Lapusnik, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, Mr. Krasniqi said when he testified that this main road was the Peja-Pristina road. This is a -- I'm going to ask you again. This is -- this is a reference to the battle of the 9th of May in Lapusnik, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be, but allow me to explain. This is -- this speaks about the main road that passes in the Pashtrik subzone is the Prizren-Pristina road which goes in the middle of Pashtrik zone and I know that various units have carried out operations in this area. The Peja-Pristina road doesn't pass through Pashtrik subzone. It passes through the Drenica Operational Zone and Dukadjin Operational Zone. But the Pristina-Prizren runs in the middle of Pashtrik subzone and the KLA units have carried out operations in various places along this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where -- where along that road -- where along that road did they carried out operations, on the Peja-Pristina road? What villages?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Duhla there were operational actions; in Samadrazhe, from Drerdalan, from Rahovec, in the villages of Rahovec. Everywhere they could carry out such actions. On the 9th of May it refers to Drenica. Otherwise, it couldn't be. When it talks about the Lapusnik gorge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it couldn't be, you say, because you say that the Lapusnik was not in the Pashtrik zone?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for that. I can argue why, because, Your Honours, on the 9th of May, there are 10 or 15 military units of Drenica who fought from Orlat, from Gjurgjice to Lapusnik, whereas we, we were five people who went to their succour. That is why I'm saying this. That is the only logical reason. So direct, those units of -- from Gjurgjice with the commander -- Gjurgjice, they all fought. They were all -- they were all units from Drenica. So if we follow the logic it refers to them. We were only five people who, as I said, went to help them. A group that decided to go immediately to help them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, we'll get to that in due course. But first can you tell me when was the operational action that you're talking about in Duhla? When did that occur?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations, the actions that might have taken place were in Duhla, Istok. I, for example, with Ismet fought with the Serb police in Duhla. When I got injured at night, we went out and we ran into Serb ambush and we fought, and in the course of that fighting I was injured on the arm. At that time, Malisheve didn't have any other place where Serbs attacked other than Duhla or Rahovec, where Rahovec borders Malisheve or the other part that borders Kline.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you think that night that you got injured in your arm that is being referred to as "the lightning actions by our military formations" in this communique? Is that what the communique is referring to?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What do you think it's referring to, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it does, but I am telling you that they refer to the actions of the KLA. It was not Limaj. There were many other units that were involved in actions. I don't remember the names of the units because we were illegal then, underground I mean. I'm trying to give you an example. On the 29th of April, I got injured, and there is a number of activities here, mentioned here. It sums up the activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm interested in the lightning action by your military formations at the main road. Can you help us with what that is if it's not Lapusnik gorge?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this doesn't specify any particular action. This sums up various activities carried out over a time in various areas to inform the public of the activities that occurred during a certain period of time. It doesn't go into detail. One of those actions on the 26th or 29th of April, I myself got injured. But during that time there were other units that operated, units from Malisheve that operated in Duhla-Suhareke road or other places or the units of Rahovec in the road Prizren-Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's talk about the borders of the operational zone. You drew a diagram. It's DL7. You drew the borders of the operational zones. The first thing that I noticed about this diagram is that - and it can be put before you - the -- the big red triangle in the middle where the bodies were found at Berisha doesn't seem to fall within any zone according to your map, does it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. If you could repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The red triangle in the middle of the map there that's at Berisha, where the bodies of people executed were found. That doesn't, according to your map, fall into any of the three zones, does it? It falls into a little space between the three zones. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No. This is not true. I didn't have points there, here where it shows the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If it could be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. [Interpretation] May I answer your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see, Your Honours, when I drew these lines, I based on points. As you can see here, you can see the Berisha point or dot, and Divjak, and the border to which Berisha stretches is underlying there. When I say "Berisha," it does not discuss the fact that Berisha does belong to that zone. Maybe the way it is drawn gives you a wrong impression, but it is true that Berisha belonged there because it is part of Malisheve municipality. But I don't know where the exact border between the Dipjan [phoen] and Malisheve is, but Berisha was part of the Malisheve municipality and that's why I thought that wherever that village was it is part of Malisheve commune or municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And therefore, according to you, part of the Pashtrik zone; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here you can see that these villages below Likovc Baince, Shale and Kisna Reka. You can see them here below. Even when I drew the line here I based on the villages. I don't know the border between Kisna Reka and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I was only interested in Berisha.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you accept, do you not, that by the end of May, 1998, Syleman Selimi was the commander of the Drenica zone? You accept that; right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I think. In the end of May, beginning of June, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And as the commander of the Drenica zone, he knew the boundary of his zone, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't know the boundary of his zone because that line was not determined. The zones were envisaged to -- according to the municipalities. The reconstruction was made quite later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The Klina municipality was always divided between the Drenica zone and the Dukadjin zone, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Malisheve-Pashtrik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So it's not true is it that the zones were drawn along the lines of municipalities, because certain municipalities were divided into two different zones.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not true. This happened later. In the beginning, the Klina municipality was entirely under the Dukagjini operational subzone, what I know as a principle. But later on according to military logic, the zones were -- the lines were determined according to the necessity in different areas. To my knowledge, Klina, Istok at that time, as well as Peja and Jakov were in Dukagjini zone, or Erenik as it was called. I'm not quite sure. There is a dilemma here because at that time another zone, Erenik zone was envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If you could please simply answer my questions, okay? Syleman Selimi testified that in May 1998 the border of the Drenica zone was the Pristina-Peja highway, and that was true, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I refer to it the way the General Staff saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So you're saying that you knew better or you know better than Syleman Selimi about where his zone -- the border of his zone?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm referring to the General Staff and the activity that was ongoing at that time in that area. I'm referring to the General Staff and the activity at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Syleman Selimi also testified that he was appointed by the General Staff and had regular communication with the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Syleman Selimi was not designated, but he was a unit commander. And later on he was approved by the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Approved by the General Staff, appointed by the General Staff to be the commander of the Drenica zone?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And he testified that he had regular communication with the General Staff at that time.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So he would know, wouldn't he, what the border of his zone was?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you know from Mr. Krasniqi's testimony, who was member of the General Staff, why Selimi -- it wasn't clear to him what was the boundary. I don't know. In January 1999, I was part of the commission to determine the zone boundaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: January 1999?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in January 1999 I was member of the commission of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We're talking about May of 1998. If we could focus on that. Since you mentioned Mr. Krasniqi, he testified that he thought Mr. -- that Syleman Selimi knew the boundary of his zone.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He should have known the boundaries, but even for that time the fact that he didn't know or whether he knew or not was very common.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Limaj, the Pashtrik zone went up to the Peja-Pristina highway, and that was the dividing line between the Pashtrik zone and the Drenica zone, and the only reason that you are saying otherwise now is to try to put the Lapusnik village outside of your -- outside of the Pashtrik zone and put into that Syleman Selimi's zone.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your attempt to present it in this way is not true. I know your attempts, but this is absolutely not true, because my entire activity shows it different. And you will see what my military activity was, and that's why I'm saying this is not true what you're attempting to put. Here you are trying to present the division of operational zones as per main roads, but this was not true. How, for example, the Nerodime and Pashtrik zone are divided between each other. Didn't talk about the division of zones in a strict sense of the word as you are putting it to me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Even Ramadan Behluli who was just a soldier in Carraleve knew that he was in the Pashtrik zone.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ramadan Behluli was in Pashtrik zone when he became a soldier after August. But Ramadan Behluli has nothing to do with KLA until August in the sense of zones or boundaries. You know well what position Ramadan Behluli had to know such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: His his statement which is now in evidence as P119, he said that during May, June, and July he -- of 1998 he was in the Pashtrik zone. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true, absolutely not. On the contrary. It's wrong if not a lie. But I believe he made a mistake, and he has not wanted to lie. Let me give you a concrete explanation. The problem is that you have not investigated this issue thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, I'm going to move on. I'd like to look at the statement that Jakup Krasniqi made on the 14th of June, 1998. It's P139. It's not in that bundle, Mr. Limaj. You see bottom of the page there in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean "An Army That Only Knows Albanianism"? That is the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. And there's a picture of Jakup Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is -- I see a uniform, a logo of the KLA. I don't see -- yes, yes, now I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, you were standing next to Jakup Krasniqi when he made this declaration, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And he said that "The UCK General Staff is of the opinion that during the present phase political pluralism is a luxury."

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... didn't you, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is not the first thing to happen. Even Churchill has declared a similar thing. Jakup Krasniqi was not the first to utter such a statement. That is stated by the representative of the country which is a country rich in democratic traditions. So I fully complied with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: He also stated that "We are asking the United States of America and the western democracies to be seriously committed to the establishment of freedom and peace in the Balkan region." And then he talks about the UCK, "which has been able to create a broad, free territory within a short period of time and to defend and create new free territories until complete liberation occurs." And that was true, wasn't it? By then the KLA had created a broad territory in your area and in Drenica, a broad free zone; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, Malisheva was under the control of the KLA, as I have already explained. Through the statement you can see that the Malisheva was under the control of the KLA, and so we could not see them other than as free zones. From the statement, you can understand that the KLA always sought to resolve the problem through peaceful means, through political means. This shows once again the vision of the KLA, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at communique number 49 which is published a month later. It's -- in your version it's 1615 in the big format. It's U0038577 in P48. Do you find that, 1615, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get the number. Now I saw it. Just a second, please. [In English] Yes. Yes, I see. [Interpretation] I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you see it's on the bottom right of the page?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Communication By the Informative Directorate of the KLA"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. Communique number 49. And it says -- this is on the 13th of July, 1998. This is when -- again when you're regularly meeting with Jakup Krasniqi; right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the 14th of June we met frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it says: "Measures have also been taken against certain diehard collaborators who are still working against our national interests." Do you see that, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third sentence. It must be, as you say, of course, but I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll read it again?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "Measures have also been taken against certain diehard collaborators who are still working against our national interests."

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "Collaborators are people who are working against the interests of the KLA."

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's move to an interview that Jakup Krasniqi gave in Koha Ditore on the 11th of July, 1998 and it's -- I believe it's the first page of that bundle, 1603, and it's 8580 in P48. Yes? Did you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the operational zones, in the territories, I know about the place I was situated in Malisheve. There was not a -- it must have meant some other place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, Mr. -- Mr. Limaj, in fact this is on the 13th of July, 1998. In fact, on the 14th -- either the 14th or 15th of June, the 17th of June, and the 21st of June of 1998, there was fighting -- pretty intensive fighting in Carraleve, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: June.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And approximately the 25th of June there was pretty intensive fighting in Luznica, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] 25 June. [Interpretation] It may be. Yes, in that period there was intensive fighting. I don't maybe remember the exact date, but the period is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So what you just said, that there was no fighting in your area is not true. This is referring to those fights.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It says: "Our formations have successfully carried out large operations in the subzones of Pashtrik." That's what it's referring to. The fighting in Carraleve and Luznica.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Maybe the translation was not good. I had in mind something else. I had in mind Malisheve municipality. There were -- there was no fighting inside that municipality at that time. This is what I thought, but there was fighting in Blace, then around Suva Reka which borders with Malisheve. So in the Pashtrik zone there is constant fighting at that time. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I meant inside the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's move on to the Jakup Krasniqi interview.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. [Interpretation] Can you please repeat it again?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1603, 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, this is an interview that Jakup Krasniqi gave while he was in Klecke; right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not an interview given in Klecke. I can assure you that. It cannot be in Klecke. It may be either in Divjak or in his home, because when they refer to Klecke, I have in mind my base. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In Divjak.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be Divjak. We have to make a distinction here, to be clear. Either at his home, because at that time Mr. Krasniqi stayed also at his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And Shukri Buja was present during the interview, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Look at the second -- look at the second page.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I saw it. But I don't know whether -- I didn't know whether it's the same interview we are talking about. Yes. Yes. This photo is in Klecke, yes. But this other photo here doesn't show anything, whereas this photo shows Klecke because I know. I recognise the ground. This interview must have been given in Klecke then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So it was in Klecke after all?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, in my own base, in the place where I stayed all the time. But I was surprised. I was taken aback by the first photo which didn't show anything. I know that he has given interviews in many places, but from the second picture I understand that it was in Klecke.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, if you could look, it's part way -- on the English it's about halfway down on 8580 and on your version on the first page, 1603 at the bottom of the first column it says: "The Albanian political parties must recognise the UCK as the entirety of the armed forces of Kosova and recognise the present situation as a state of war." Then -- do you see that at the bottom of the first column?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm afraid I'm not finding it. I don't know what you mean, the first, the second, or the third.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The first column. Look at the first column. Go to the --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now do you see it there?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Calls on the political parties to unite and to form a front, join the KLA." Yes. This is what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. It says -- yes. It says: "The political parties must recognise the UCK as the entirety of the armed forces of Kosova, recognise the present situation as a state of war." You see that now?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It's at the end. It means the political parties that operate in Kosova, they should recognise the KLA as entirety of the armed forces and recognise the current situation as a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you would look at the next column, the second column.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The end of Mr. Krasniqi's answer at the bottom of that column. Okay?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It says: "The UCK is a liberation army and a regular military formation. It is not an organisation or group that goes in for small-scale actions. Our operations are rather large and bear a greater resemblance to those of a regular army." Do you see that, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you see -- look at -- there's a second day of the interview. If you go to the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the 12th of July? I see here the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Look at 1605.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second. Let me find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You were just looking at 1603. So it's 1605.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see 1604 with a photo of Shukri.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: 1605, please.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then give me a second to find it. I see 1603 and 1604 here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, we'll give you a small version of it.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it. I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, if you would look at the beginning of the interview, the second day of this interview. The beginning of the first column it says: "The UCK is a new army in the process of formation. However, the UCK has had its own staff and its military hierarchy from the start and still has today." You see that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Then he says -- at the end of that answer he says: "The UCK is an organised army." You see that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That was true at the time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What can I add to the answer or to the statement made by Mr. Krasniqi? This is not true. This is not true. You had here the author of this interview. It's not true. The facts on the ground speak for themselves. He might have said what he wished. I can give you details about what I know, but this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many international observers have said the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Limaj, you have said that by the middle of June -- by the middle of June 1998, the KLA was organised, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said it differently. I said the organisation begins -- Jakupi came around the beginning and mid of July to organise something in Pashtrik zone. But you know how long it takes for an organisation to take place. A branch of a political party -- to set up a branch of the political party takes a week at least. I have said this is the beginning, when we see the first nomination of zone commander for the process to go on. This is what I said.
